nodes.description: NHLRC2 comprises an N-terminal thioredoxin-like (Trx-like) domain, a six-bladed NHL repeat beta-propeller domain, and a C-terminal beta-stranded domain. Pathogenic missense variants such as p.Asp148Tyr in the Trx-like domain thermally destabilize the protein structure by 2 degrees Celsius and markedly reduce steady-state cellular NHLRC2 protein levels. Combined with null or hypomorphic second alleles, total cellular NHLRC2 falls below critical functional thresholds, with more severe depletion driving early multisystem and pulmonary disease.

evidence.reference_title: Variant in NHLRC2 leads to increased hnRNP C2 in developing neurons and the hippocampus of a mouse model of FINCA disease.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, isoform C2 of hnRNP C1/C2 was significantly increased in both developing neurons and the hippocampus of adult female FINCA mice, connecting NHLRC2 dysfunction with accumulation of RNA binding protein.

evidence.reference_title: Variant in NHLRC2 leads to increased hnRNP C2 in developing neurons and the hippocampus of a mouse model of FINCA disease.
evidence.snippet: The increase in the hnRNP C2 protein in Nhlrc2FINCA/− embryonic NPCs and adult mouse hippocampus suggests a perturbation in overall RNA metabolism, which in turn may contribute to the neurodegeneration seen in FINCA disease.

nodes.description: Homozygous Nhlrc2 null mouse embryos arrest prior to the morula stage, demonstrating that complete loss of NHLRC2 is embryonic lethal.

Compound heterozygous FINCA mouse model carrying the patient-equivalent missense variant p.Asp148Tyr combined with a null allele. Mice are viable and exhibit adolescent hyperactivity, decreased exploration of novel objects, altered innate immune interferon-gamma responses, dysregulated Rho GTPase signaling, vesicular trafficking defects, and accumulation of hnRNP C2 in developing neurons and adult female hippocampus.

nodes.description: Red blood cell transfusions are frequently required during infancy to manage severe macrocytic and dyserythropoietic anemia.

evidence.reference_title: Novel patients with NHLRC2 variants expand the phenotypic spectrum of FINCA disease.
evidence.snippet: Laboratory investigations (Table 2) revealed macrocytic anemia in all five patients, with the bone marrow aspirates in two patients (patients five and six, Table 2) showing increased erythropoiesis or dyserythropoiesis, marked bi- and multinuclearity of erythroblasts and increased eosinophils suggestive of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (CDA type II) (Figures 3A, B). Four out of five patients needed several red blood cell transfusions in infancy. Furthermore, immunodeficiency with decreased immunoglobulin levels was detected in two patients.

nodes.description: Progressive fibrotic remodeling of the pulmonary interstitium accompanied by granuloma-like lung lesions, ground-glass opacities, and pulmonary consolidations, leading to severe infantile interstitial lung disease and hypoxemic respiratory failure.

evidence.reference_title: NHLRC2 variants identified in patients with fibrosis, neurodegeneration, and cerebral angiomatosis (FINCA): characterisation of a novel cerebropulmonary disease.
evidence.snippet: Interstitial fibrosis and previously undescribed granuloma-like lesions were observed in the lungs. Hepatomegaly, steatosis and collagen accumulation were detected in the liver.

evidence.reference_title: Case Report: Clinical manifestations and treatment of two Chinese patients with FINCA syndrome carrying a novel variant of NHLRC2.
evidence.snippet: About half of the 31 FINCA patients presented with respiratory symptoms, such as tachypnea, cough, hypoxemia, and respiratory distress. Chest CT scans were performed on 11 patients, among whom 9 children were diagnosed with ILD, with the most prevalent findings being GGOs and pulmonary consolidations.

nodes.description: Recurrent respiratory tract infections beginning in infancy, often triggering exacerbations of interstitial lung disease and anemia.

evidence.reference_title: Novel patients with NHLRC2 variants expand the phenotypic spectrum of FINCA disease.
evidence.snippet: All five patients presented with multiorgan dysfunction with neurodevelopmental delay, recurrent infections and macrocytic anemia as key features. Interstitial lung disease was pronounced in infancy but often stabilized.

nodes.description: Tachypnea, cough, hypoxemia, and progressive respiratory distress or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) presenting in about half of reported FINCA patients during infancy.

nodes.description: Focal and generalized seizures occurring in 11 of 15 patients in the largest series (onset 9 months to 13 years), which may progress to status epilepticus.

evidence.reference_title: Broadening the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of FINCA syndrome: Biallelic NHLRC2 variants in 15 novel individuals.
evidence.snippet: All 15 individuals had variable neuromuscular involvement: 12 had truncal hypotonia, five individuals were never able to walk and four developed hyperkinetic movement disorder, spasticity or hyperreflexia. Two depended on a wheelchair for long distances and five had an unsteady, wide gait. Seizures occurred in 11 individuals, with age of onset ranging from nine months to 13 years.

evidence.reference_title: FINCA syndrome-Defining neurobehavioral phenotype in survivors into late childhood.
evidence.snippet: Two girls have epilepsy with focal and generalized seizures that are not frequent however, may lead to status epilepticus.

nodes.description: Pyramidal tract involvement with spasticity and hyperreflexia developing in a subset of affected children alongside movement disorders.

nodes.description: Long-term systemic glucocorticoid therapy can improve respiratory symptoms, chest CT findings, and serum KL-6 levels in patients with FINCA-associated interstitial lung disease.

evidence.reference_title: Case Report: Clinical manifestations and treatment of two Chinese patients with FINCA syndrome carrying a novel variant of NHLRC2.
evidence.snippet: The elder brother died of infantile respiratory failure, while the younger brother showed improvement in respiratory symptoms, chest CT, and Krebs von den Lungen-6 levels after long-term systemic glucocorticoid therapy, indicating that anti-inflammatory treatment may be beneficial in the treatment of ILD caused by FINCA syndrome.

nodes.description: Hypoplasia or atrophy of the corpus callosum observed on brain MRI.

evidence.reference_title: Novel patients with NHLRC2 variants expand the phenotypic spectrum of FINCA disease.
evidence.snippet: Chest radiography showed ARDS and chronic pneumonitis, with brain MRI revealing atrophy of the corpus callosum. A severe general cerebral and cerebellar atrophy in a patient at the age of 17 years suggested progressive neurodegeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Broadening the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of FINCA syndrome: Biallelic NHLRC2 variants in 15 novel individuals.
evidence.snippet: Brain abnormalities (dilated ventricles, corpus callosum hypoplasia, mild cortical atrophy and delayed myelination) were diagnosed in five individuals, while six had unremarkable brain MRI scans.

nodes.description: Progressive vacuolar degeneration and neuronal depletion across the cerebral cortex, cerebellum, and spinal cord anterior horns, resulting in progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy and severe neurodevelopmental impairment.

evidence.reference_title: NHLRC2 variants identified in patients with fibrosis, neurodegeneration, and cerebral angiomatosis (FINCA): characterisation of a novel cerebropulmonary disease.
evidence.snippet: In the affected children, neuropathology revealed increased angiomatosis-like leptomeningeal, cortical and superficial white matter vascularisation and congestion, vacuolar degeneration and myelin loss in white matter, as well as neuronal degeneration.

evidence.snippet: Neuropathology of FINCA patients identified brain atrophy, vacuolar neurodegeneration, myelin loss with gliosis, cerebral angiomatosis, and neuronal depletion of the anterior horns of the spinal cord (Uusimaa et al. 2018).
